chapter: Kansas City, Omaha and Lloyd Hunter
title: Black union local 627 and who could sit in
summary: Gus explains the Black local 627 in Kansas City, its president Shaw and how a ten-cent beer bought a blind eye to sitting in.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: : When did you join the union?
I joined -- I had the union --
: There were two unions at that time, weren't there?
And I couldn't sit in and play, no way. The president of the union would come by and he wouldn't want you to sit in and play with anybody, unless you joined the union.
And still they didn't want you to play.
All you had to do is buy a ten-cent beer, and he'd turn his head. So I got by with all of that.
Well, (unintelligible) sit in as long as you belonged.
Well, you might be knocking somebody out -- somebody else out of a job, see, one of those things.
Well, it was one of those things in the union.
-- he would -- his name was Shaw, the president of the union.
Yeah. How long was it before those two unions --
It hasn't been too long, I'll tell you that.
When they merged -- Kansas City and the white union merged together. Like Chicago, the same thing.
But 802, they'd been merged, it was always like that.
Yeah. Well, so Joe was unquestionably must have been impressed if he meets you right away and then says to you, Of course, he just dug perceived that you swung.
